passage.title: Reading Part 2 - Test 03
passage.text:
Social media has revolutionized the way people communicate in the 21st century. Platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram have connected billions of users worldwide, allowing them to share information, ideas, and experiences instantly. While these platforms have brought many benefits, they have also raised important questions about privacy, mental health, and the quality of human interaction.

One of the most significant advantages of social media is its ability to connect people across vast distances. Families separated by geography can now stay in touch daily through video calls and photo sharing. Professional networks like LinkedIn have made it easier for people to find jobs and build careers. Additionally, social media has given a voice to marginalized groups who previously had limited access to public platforms. Movements for social justice have used these tools to organize protests and raise awareness about important issues.

However, critics argue that social media has also created serious problems. Studies have shown that excessive use of social media can lead to anxiety, depression, and feelings of inadequacy, particularly among young people who constantly compare themselves to others online. The curated nature of social media posts—where people share only their best moments—creates an unrealistic picture of life that can be harmful. Furthermore, the spread of misinformation and "fake news" on these platforms has become a major concern, as false information can reach millions of people before it can be corrected.

Another issue is the impact on face-to-face communication. Some researchers suggest that as people spend more time interacting online, they are losing important social skills needed for in-person conversations. The nuances of body language, tone of voice, and facial expressions are absent in text-based communication, which can lead to misunderstandings. Despite these challenges, social media continues to evolve, and society must find ways to maximize its benefits while minimizing its negative effects.
